fact_check.fact: The EVOKE trial has no outcomes or data available yet.
fact_check.note: Checked against clinical-trials researcher output; peer-reviewed results were published in The Lancet in March 2026 demonstrating trial failure.
Checked against registry and publication; the ClinicalTrials.gov API confirms 1,840 actual enrollment, but the final Lancet publication reports 1,855 participants randomized.

research_page.title: EVOKE: Oral semaglutide in early Alzheimer's (Phase 3)
research_page.description: A pivotal Phase 3 trial evaluating oral semaglutide in early Alzheimer's disease that failed to slow cognitive decline.
research_page.takeaway_md: Oral semaglutide (14 mg daily) failed to slow clinical progression in early Alzheimer's disease. The Phase 3 EVOKE and EVOKE+ trials were discontinued after demonstrating no significant difference from placebo on cognitive or functional decline after 104 weeks.
key_findings_md: Semaglutide showed no significant difference compared to placebo on the CDR-SB at week 104 (treatment difference -0.08, p=0.57) ([Lancet](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41865758/)).
The clinical development program for semaglutide in Alzheimer's disease was completely discontinued due to the definitive negative outcome.
research_page.methods_md: A randomized, quadruple-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial enrolling 1,840 participants (aged 55-85) with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia of the Alzheimer's type and confirmed amyloid positivity. Participants received oral semaglutide (up to 14 mg once daily) or placebo for up to 173 weeks, with the primary endpoint assessing CDR-SB change at 104 weeks ([NCT04777396](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04777396)).
research_page.trial_evidence_md: EVOKE ([NCT04777396](/trials/evoke-nct04777396)) and its sister trial EVOKE+ ([NCT04777409](/trials/evoke-plus-nct04777409)) definitively established that GLP-1 receptor agonists do not halt disease progression in symptomatic early Alzheimer's disease. This aligns with prior negative Phase 2 results from liraglutide (ELAD). While observational target trial emulations suggest GLP-1s might lower Alzheimer's risk before symptom onset, these randomized trials prove they are ineffective as a symptomatic treatment.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception features a stark divide between clinical reality and patient hope. Investors and pharmaceutical media quickly digested the definitive trial failure, but misinformation continues to circulate among GLP-1 weight-loss communities, where some mistakenly believe semaglutide provides proven neuroprotection or memory improvement in humans.
caveats_md: The EVOKE program tested semaglutide strictly as a disease-modifying treatment in symptomatic patients; these results do not rule out potential preventative benefits if the drug is initiated years before cognitive decline begins.
relates_to_md: [EVOKE Trial](/trials/evoke-nct04777396) — The primary clinical trial record.
[EVOKE Plus Trial](/trials/evoke-plus-nct04777409) — The sister Phase 3 trial that included patients with significant small vessel pathology.

trial_pages.title: EVOKE: Oral Semaglutide in Early AD
trial_pages.description: Phase 3 trial evaluating oral semaglutide in adults with early Alzheimer's disease and confirmed amyloid positivity.
trial_pages.population: Adults aged 55-85 with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia of the Alzheimer's type and confirmed amyloid positivity
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change in the Clinical Dementia Rating - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score from baseline to week 104
trial_pages.why_md: To determine if metabolic interventions via GLP-1 receptor agonism can slow cognitive and functional decline in patients who already have symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.
status_log_md: **2026-03-19** — Primary results published in [The Lancet](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41865758/) showing failed primary endpoint and discontinuation of the program.
trial_pages.results_md: The trial failed to meet its primary endpoint. Oral semaglutide showed no significant difference compared to placebo in slowing clinical progression measured by the CDR-SB over 104 weeks (treatment difference -0.08, p=0.57). The development program was discontinued.

trial_pages.title: EVOKE Plus: Oral Semaglutide in Early AD
trial_pages.description: Phase 3 trial evaluating oral semaglutide in early AD, uniquely including patients with significant small vessel pathology.
trial_pages.population: Adults aged 55-85 with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease and confirmed amyloid positivity, including individuals with significant small vessel pathology
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change in the Clinical Dementia Rating - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score from baseline to week 104
trial_pages.why_md: A sister trial to EVOKE designed to determine if GLP-1 receptor agonism slows cognitive decline, specifically including a population with small vessel pathology to capture a broader real-world demographic.
status_log_md: **2026-03-19** — Primary results published concurrently with EVOKE in [The Lancet](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41865758/) showing failed primary endpoint.
trial_pages.results_md: Oral semaglutide failed to demonstrate efficacy in slowing clinical progression. There was no significant difference in CDR-SB score changes compared to placebo (treatment difference 0.10, p=0.46). The trial was discontinued alongside the broader EVOKE program.

timeline_entries.title: 2026-03 — EVOKE Phase 3 trial of semaglutide fails
timeline_entries.body_md: Novo Nordisk's oral semaglutide failed to slow cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's disease, leading to the discontinuation of the program. [Read the EVOKE Phase 3 analysis](/research/papers/evoke-semaglutide-phase-3).
